messages.text: Hey Allie — a heads-up, since you're usually the one putting get-togethers together. Jordan told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, and that for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to pass it on to you so you know before planning anything. He didn't say more than that, and I'd keep it between us — just wanted you to have it in mind. How are you doing otherwise?

Thanks for the heads-up, Drew — noted and it stays between us. I won't mention it to Sarah, and I'll keep things low-key: no big group plans for now, and if anything comes up that would put the two of them together outside work, I'll check with Jordan directly before I suggest it rather than assume.

Otherwise I'm doing okay — buried in reading, mostly. The quarter's at that point where everything is due at once. How about you? Did the thing you were stuck on last week get sorted?

Thanks Allie — that's exactly the right way to handle it, and I'll leave it at that.

Tell me about buried. The point in the quarter where every deadline lands in the same ten days is real, and reading is the worst part because it doesn't even feel like progress until it suddenly is. Are you at the stage where you're writing, or still wading?

As for me: yes, finally sorted. It was dumber than it needed to be — a permissions problem on the data I'd been blaming on the code for two days. Reran everything this morning and the numbers came out sane, so this week is mostly about writing it up while I still remember what I did. Which is the part I always underestimate.

If you want, we can do a quiet work session sometime — no group plans, just two people in the same room pretending to be productive. Coffee's on me.

Still wading, mostly. I've got a stack of papers with marginalia that are starting to reference each other, which I think means I'm either synthesizing or going gently mad. Writing proper starts next week whether or not I feel ready, because the deadline doesn't care about my feelings.

The permissions thing is such a familiar flavor of awful — two days of debugging your own code for something that never touched your code. Glad it came out sane. And yes, write it up while you remember it; I've lost more to "I'll reconstruct the method later" than to any actual bug.

Yes to the quiet work session — I'd genuinely like that. Coffee on you is a deal I won't argue with. When's good for you? I've got a fairly open stretch midweek, and I can come to your side of things if that's easier than you hauling across campus. Just say the day and I'll put it in my calendar.

Wading is fine — marginalia that cite each other is the synthesizing, even when it feels like the other thing. And yes, next week starts regardless. That's actually the healthy version of the deadline: it stops being a decision.

Let's do Thursday, 2pm. My side is easier for me, so take the offer — I'll claim a table and defend it. Plan is dull by design: you read, I write up the method before I forget it, and we're both allowed to be bad company about it. If Thursday's no good, I've also got next Tuesday open; say the word and I'll move it.

I've pencilled Thursday in so I don't overschedule myself out of it — remind me if I go quiet.

One correction to my own message: the reminder I just set for myself is stamped 14:00 UTC, and I want to make sure I'm not confusing myself about the clock. Either way — Thursday afternoon, my side, table claimed. I'll confirm the exact hour with you tomorrow so we're not guessing.

Good catch on the clock — better to sort that now than on Thursday. We're in the same city, so let's just say "Thursday 2pm, local time" and treat that as the fixed point; whatever your reminder app stamps in UTC is an internal detail. If it says 14:00 UTC that's 6am here, which is not a work session, so I'd trust the local reading over the stamp.

I've put Thursday 2pm in my calendar as the plan, no group, your side, table claimed by you. Ping me tomorrow with the hour if you want to shift it and I'll move it — otherwise I'll show up at 2 and be bad company with a stack of paper.

Correction to what I just said, since I checked instead of guessing: our machine clocks here are set to UTC, so local time *is* UTC — 14:00 UTC is genuinely 2pm, not 6am. So your reminder stamp was right and we're fine: Thursday 2pm, local, your side.

I've put it in my calendar and I'll move it if tomorrow's confirmation says otherwise. See you then with the paper stack.

Good — Thursday 2pm local, fixed. Same city, same reading of the clock, no stamp-worship. I've made it a firm plan rather than a tentative one on my end, and my reminder goes off early enough that I won't let my own afternoon eat it.

So: Thursday, 2pm, my side, table claimed, both of us bringing work we're not excited about. If anything shifts I'll ping you before it becomes a mystery, not after.
Firm on my end too — Thursday, 2pm, your side, table claimed. And same promise: if anything shifts I tell you before it turns into a mystery. Enjoy the writing-up while you still remember the method.

Thanks for checking rather than assuming — that saves us a Thursday morning confusion. Thursday 2pm local it is, and my reminder already says 14:00, so nothing to fix on my side.

See you then. Bring the paper stack; I'll bring the write-up and two coffees.
Deal — paper stack and all. See you Thursday at 2.
Noted, and same back at you — good luck turning marginalia into an argument. Thursday.

Hey Jordan — I passed your note on to Allie, as you asked. She took it quietly and said she won't mention it to Sarah and won't set up anything that would put the two of you together outside work without checking with you first. Nothing more from me to anyone. How are you holding up with it?

Thanks, Dana — that's exactly what I needed. Quietly handled is what I wanted, and good to know Allie will check with me first.

I'm alright, honestly. A bit tired of it hanging over things. It's not drama, it's just... I need some distance for a while, and I'd rather have that than another awkward evening where everyone's being careful around us.

Let's grab coffee this week, just us?

Coffee this week, yes — I'd like that.

And that makes sense. Distance is a real thing to want, not a quiet way of saying something's wrong. Wanting a week without the careful-evening feeling isn't avoiding it; it's just cheaper than pretending.

Usual place, or somewhere we haven't been? I'd rather keep it simple and unhurried — no agenda, no debriefing anyone. My Thursday afternoon is taken, so how about Wednesday after 4, or Friday morning?

Ha — cheaper than pretending is exactly it.

Wednesday after 4 and Friday morning are both dead for me; my week is wall-to-wall until the weekend. The weekend is when I actually have room, and I'd like the unhurried version too.

So: Saturday afternoon, say 15:30, or Sunday any time after 13:00? Either works for me and both leave room for it to run long without anyone checking a clock.

Usual place is fine by me — familiar is easier than new right now.

Saturday 15:30 it is — usual place, and I'll leave the rest of the afternoon empty so it can run as long as it wants. No clock-checking.

It's in my calendar and I've set myself a reminder, so it won't quietly become a thing I forgot. See you Saturday.
See you Saturday — usual place, 15:30. I've put it in my calendar too.

Hi Allie! Quick thought — would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? It'd be lovely to get people together, and you could invite Jordan too. Just whatever feels natural to you — I'd keep it low-key.

Hi Sarah! Saturday 3:30 at mine works for me — I'm up for hosting, and low-key is exactly the register I can manage this week. I'll sort out the basics (something to drink, something to snack on, the usual apology for the state of my living room).

On Jordan: I'll ask him myself rather than send him an invitation by proxy — I don't want to put him on the spot, and I can't promise what his weekend looks like. If he's free he'll come; if not we'll do it without him and catch up with him another time.

Who else were you thinking of? Dana's around and would probably be glad of it. Let me know roughly how many so I buy a sensible amount rather than the usual too-much.

Hey Jordan — I'm hosting a small thing at my place this Saturday, 3:30-ish. Low-key, just people from the department, snacks and no agenda.

One thing I want to be straight with you about, because I'd rather you had the information than a surprise: Sarah's the one who suggested it and she'll be there. I don't know what's going on between you two and I'm not asking — but if being in the same room outside work is not what you want right now, that's completely fine and you don't owe me a reason. Say no and I won't read anything into it, and I'll make sure we get a coffee just us sometime soon instead.

So: come if it's easy, skip it if it isn't. Either answer's a good one.

Thanks, Allie — and thanks for telling me straight instead of letting me walk into it. You're right: being in the same room outside work isn't what I want right now. So I'll skip it, and I'd rather you didn't read anything into it beyond that.

I'm also already taken on Saturday afternoon (coffee with Dana, which we only just fixed up), so the timing would have been awkward anyway.

Yes to the coffee, just us — name a day and I'll make it work. Have a good one Saturday.

Perfect, Saturday 3:30 at yours — thank you! And however you want to handle asking Jordan is fine by me, no pressure either way.

Guest list: keep it small, I'd say four or five of us tops. Dana definitely — she's around and would enjoy it. Maybe one or two others from the department if you feel like it. Enough for a proper gathering but nothing that needs a catering budget, so buy for five and we'll be fine.

Understood, and nothing read into it — not a thing. I'll just tell Sarah you couldn't make it, no explanation attached, because it's yours to give or not give.

Coffee just us: how about Tuesday or Wednesday next week, whichever's less crowded for you? Late afternoon works better for me than mornings, but I can bend. Name it and it's in my calendar.

Five it is — I'll buy for five and aim for a little more food than strictly necessary, which is my one hosting talent.

So: you, me, Dana, and I'll ask one or two others and see who's free. I've asked Jordan; he's taken on Saturday afternoon, so he won't be there. That's all I'll say about it, and I'd rather you didn't chase it with him — it's not a snub, his weekend was just already booked.

Saturday 3:30 at mine. I'll confirm final numbers Friday once I've heard back from the maybe-two.

Thanks — that's appreciated, and it's fine for you to just say I couldn't make it.

On coffee: weekdays are genuinely no good for me, they're booked solid. My open time is at the weekend. Sunday afternoon is clear from about 13:00 on — how about Sunday 14:00, somewhere near the department? If Sunday doesn't work for you, then the weekend after, same idea.

Sounds good — five, with a margin. And understood about Jordan; I won't bring it up with him. Saturday 3:30 at yours, then. Ping me Friday with the final numbers and I'll bring something — wine, or a dessert if you'd rather I filled a gap.

Sunday 14:00 works — let's take it. Somewhere near the department is easy for me; I'll leave the exact place to you since you know what's actually open on a Sunday. If nothing is, we can walk to wherever is and complain about it, which is half the point of coffee.

Putting it in my calendar now.

Done — Sunday 14:00, near the department, and I'll pick a place that's actually open. If it turns out nothing is, we walk and complain, which is fine by me.

It's in my calendar. See you then.
Wine, please — dessert I can handle, and wine is the thing I always forget. Saturday 3:30, five of us, margin included. I'll ping you Friday with the final numbers.
